_names: Terminologia Anatomica individual terms (explicitly public domain)
_geometry: Classical thresholding + position on public-domain CT; no neural segmenter
_why_no_lobes: Measured on this volume: lung parenchyma is -540 to -570 HU where live clinical lung is -700 to -850, because a cadaver's lungs were never inflated (the fresh pre-freezing series measures the same). Lobar fissures are not resolvable, so LOBES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED.
_why_no_sides: Two independent landmarks disagree on this cadaver about which image side is the patient's left (lung asymmetry says one thing, heart position the other, on an 8% margin that flips sign). NO SIDE IS ASSERTED ANYWHERE. A missing distinction is a gap; a wrong side teaches wrong anatomy.
_why_no_levels: Position alone cannot number an individual rib or vertebral level, so structures are named generically.

lung.name: Lung
lung.definition: The lungs are the essential organs of respiration, occupying the pleural cavities on either side of the mediastinum. Each is conical, with an apex reaching above the first rib and a concave base resting on the diaphragm.

rib.name: Rib
rib.definition: The ribs are elastic arches of bone forming the greater part of the thoracic skeleton. They are twelve in number on either side, articulating behind with the vertebral column.

sternum.name: Sternum
sternum.definition: The sternum is a flat narrow bone forming the middle of the anterior wall of the thorax, consisting of the manubrium, the body and the xiphoid process.

thoracic-vertebra.name: Thoracic vertebra
thoracic-vertebra.definition: The thoracic vertebrae are twelve in number and are distinguished by the costal facets on the sides of their bodies for articulation with the heads of the ribs.

vertebral-canal.name: Vertebral canal
vertebral-canal.definition: The vertebral canal is formed by the vertebral foramina in series and contains the spinal cord with its meninges and vessels.

_why_rib_cap: Ten identical 'Rib' labels per slice saturate both gutters and add no information beyond the first few. The four largest cross-sections are kept.
